recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what ∩ asks you to keep, and how you would get A ∩ B ∩ C from the pairwise answers.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the three pairwise intersections
steps.margin_note: First mark. All three parts (i), (ii) and (iii) share this mark, so number each answer and give each its own line.
lines: A ∩ B keeps only the members that are in A and also in B.

recall.must_convey: That the intersection keeps the common members, giving {2, 4, 6, 7}, {1, 3, 5, 7} and {7}.
accept: intersection keeps only the members in both sets
A cap B is two four six seven and A cap C is one three five seven
B cap C is just seven
rendu sets lo unde common elements matrame teesukovali
check each member of the smaller set against the other set

steps.why: Each intersection is read off by testing the members of the shorter set against the longer one, so nothing has to be computed and the answers can be written straight down.
common_mistakes: Giving the union {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11} in place of A ∩ B.
Keeping 8 or 11 in A ∩ B — both are in B but neither is in A.
Writing B ∩ C = ∅ after missing 7, which is a member of both.
steps.memory_tip: ∩ has the shape of the letter n — read it as 'and', the members that both sets hold.

steps.label: Find the intersection of all three sets
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Show the line (A ∩ B) ∩ C before the answer, so the method is on the page and not only the result.
lines: A ∩ B ∩ C = (A ∩ B) ∩ C, so use the answer to part (i).

recall.must_convey: That A ∩ B is intersected with C to give {7}.
accept: take A cap B from part one and intersect it with C
the only member in all three sets is seven
seven is the answer because it is in A and B and C
modati answer ni C tho intersect cheste seven vasthundi
intersect two of them first then the third

steps.why: Intersection is associative, so any two sets may be taken first. Reusing the answer to part (i) saves testing all seven members of A a second time.
common_mistakes: Intersecting A with B ∪ C instead of with B ∩ C.
Writing the answer as the number 7 rather than as the set {7}.
Starting again from A, B and C and dropping 7 by mistake.
steps.memory_tip: Intersect any two sets first, then bring in the third — the order does not change the answer.
